en.title: Farming
en.summary: Crops, animals and the farming year, with the language of processes.

paragraphs: Farming shapes the British and American landscape. This lesson describes the main types of farming and the work that goes on through the year.

Most of the land in the United Kingdom is used for farming. Arable farms grow wheat and barley, dairy farms produce milk, and hill farms keep sheep. In the United States, the Midwest produces corn and soybeans, and vast ranches in the West raise cattle. Modern farms use machines, and fewer people work on the land than before. A farmer talks to a visitor.

lines.speaker: Visitor
lines.text: What do you grow on this farm?

lines.speaker: Farmer
lines.text: Wheat and barley. We also keep sheep and a few cows.

lines.speaker: Farmer
lines.text: Very. We get up at five every day, and in harvest time we work until midnight.

lines.speaker: Farmer
lines.text: It decides everything. If it rains too much, the crop can be spoiled.

lines.speaker: Farmer
lines.text: No. I've farmed all my life, and I wouldn't change it.

paragraphs: **1. Grow, keep and raise.** Crops are grown; animals are kept or raised. See Introduction to Grammar: Verbs and verb phrases.

blocks.html:
VerbExample
growWe grow wheat.
keepWe keep sheep.
raiseThey raise cattle on ranches.
harvestWe harvest the crop in August.

paragraphs: **2. The first conditional predicts a likely result.** If + present simple, will + base verb. See Introduction to Grammar: Moods, command, subjunctive and conditional.

blocks.html:
If-clauseResult
If it rains too much,the crop will be spoiled.
If the weather is dry,we will harvest early.
If prices fall,farmers will lose money.
If we have a good year,we'll buy a new tractor.

items: Most of the UK's land is used for farming.
Arable farming means growing crops; dairy farms produce milk.
A crop is a plant grown for food; livestock are farm animals.
A harvest is the gathering of the crop.

paragraphs: Farming in Britain is now partly supported by government payments, which also reward farmers for protecting wildlife. Farm shops and farmers' markets let visitors buy directly from the producer.
